entries.text: Something crackled back on his dish. It almost sounded like an answer.
Sent into deep space: "Little Dart is at eight percent and the stars look awfully close tonight. Can you hear me out there?"
aiming the brass dish straight into the glittering dark and tapping out a five-note call
entries.why: someone out there has to be listening to my star charts tonight.
entries.detail: Little Dart is at eight percent and the stars look awfully close tonight. Can you hear me out there?

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Night Signals from the Tower"
Idea: paint the hull of the Little Dart in non-reflective matte black to confuse the cargo-hauler bot
Read "Paint Maker ADAS Radar Optimized Color Resources: AkzoNobel": radar transparent paint formulas cannot be manually tinted or adjusted without messing up the sensors.
searching the wire for radar absorbent paint formulas
entries.why: need to check radar formulas before coating the hull

digging through cargo crate spill at the edge of the dunes
entries.why: that fallen freighter crate might have some heavy-duty copper wire for the Little Dart!

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "quick recharge in the dock"

tightening copper terminals on a busted fuel manifold for a passing hauler
entries.why: finishing up this last wiring job earns me enough credits for some fresh wire.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Wrapping up Gribble's manifold!"

soldering copper leads on a sputtering moisture filter
entries.why: a few more credits will buy that copper wire bundle for the cockpit instruments.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Credits and Copper"

tightening copper terminals on a trader's moisture condenser

Dug up a mystery box that hums and named it Gus; a scorched heat tile and named it Lorna.
rummaging through bins of old connectors at the market

checking out radar cross sections on the wire with a spinning brass dish

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Radar Cross Sections"

Read "Mie scattering - Wikipedia": light bounces off tiny spherical dust specks depending on how wide they are compared to the beam.
omlc.org wouldn't open, so he tried en.wikipedia.org instead.
checking mie scattering theory details on the comms dish screen
entries.why: need to know how those dust wavelengths behave before testing flight paths.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Mie scattering equations checked!"

Read "Mie Scattering - DRI - Light Scattering Database": light bouncing off dust depends entirely on how big the grains are and what wavelength hits them.
spinning brass dish, searching wire for scattering equations
entries.why: i want to check those mie scattering equations before the sun comes up.
